She boarded the 14:00 National Express coach at Bay 9 without checking the windscreen board, and woke up two hours later on the way to Dover Docks.

place: a diplomatic mail depot in London
situation: Canvas diplomatic bags sealed with lead stamps are exempt from X-ray scanning under international convention and must be accompanied onto the aircraft by a courier.

place: a campsite laundry in the Pyrenees
situation: Brass tokens for the washing machines can only be bought at the bread van between eight and nine in the morning, though washing powder is dispensed automatically.

place: an aircraft de-icing bay in Helsinki
who: passengers looking out of the cabin windows
situation: Before take-off in snow, the wings are sprayed first with hot orange glycol to melt frost and then with thick green fluid that shears off as the plane accelerates.

place: a youth hostel kitchen in Ljubljana
situation: Any food left on the communal fridge shelves without a name and checkout date written in marker pen is declared 'free for all' at nine o'clock every morning.

place: a cruise-ship tender pier in Santorini
situation: Numbered tender tickets are handed out in the theatre from eight a.m., and independent passengers are called only after the ship's own excursion coaches have filled up.
He booked the last lower berth at the back of the bus, which turned out to be twenty centimetres shorter than his legs because the engine housing rose underneath.

place: a customs shed at Tilbury in 1954
situation: Every seaman's sea chest was chalked with a white cross by the customs rummage crew once his tobacco allowance and watch had been declared.

place: an airport lounge shower suite in Singapore
who: a passenger halfway between Sydney and London
situation: You leave your crumpled linen shirt in a wooden cupboard inside the shower door, and a steward presses it from the corridor side and hangs it back in ten minutes.

who: twenty passengers watching the departures board
situation: The platform number for the Venice fast train was changed from Track 3 to Track 11 three minutes before arrival, sending sixty people sprinting down the subway with wheelie cases.

place: a lighthouse guesthouse on Clare Island
who: four guests cut off by a swell
situation: When the afternoon mailboat could not berth because of the Atlantic swell, the guests were given an extra night's bed and breakfast on the house and taught to bake soda farls.
